identity.wheat: The catalogue says 'Wheat'; the profile uses durum wheat (USDA 'Wheat, durum'). Other wheat differs.
identity.lettuce: Catalogue name covers Bibb, Boston and romaine; the USDA record is cos/romaine only.
identity.mushrooms: Catalogue name says 'button, shiitake'; the USDA record is white (button) mushrooms only.
identity.nut-butter: Catalogue says 'Nut butter'; the USDA record is smooth peanut butter without salt. Almond and other nut butters differ.
identity.sourdough-bread: USDA has no sourdough-only record; the record is 'Bread, french or vienna (includes sourdough)'.
identity.mint: Catalogue 'Mint' uses the USDA spearmint record; peppermint is a separate profile.
identity.kefir: The USDA record is a branded product (Lifeway, lowfat, plain). Other kefir varies.
identity.tofu: Calcium depends on the setting agent; the record is firm tofu set with calcium sulfate.
identity.hummus: Commercial hummus; salt, oil and tahini vary by brand.
identity.salsa: Ready-to-serve salsa with salt; brands vary.
identity.granola: The USDA record is homemade granola; commercial products differ.
identity.shrimp: The USDA record 'may contain additives to retain moisture', which raises its sodium.
identity.red-snapper: Mixed-species USDA record; species differ in mercury.
identity.sea-bass: Mixed-species USDA record; species differ in mercury (the caution says so).
identity.canned-tuna: Light tuna in water; albacore (white) tuna differs in mercury.
identity.tuna: Same USDA record as canned light tuna; consider merging or distinguishing the two entries.
identity.squash: 'Winter squash, all varieties' average; varieties differ.
identity.white-potato: Baked flesh and skin; boiled or fried potato differs.

servingState.oat: Serving is dry rolled oats; a bowl of porridge has far fewer nutrients per gram.
servingState.wheat-flour: Serving is flour, not a baked food.
servingState.red-lentil: Serving is dry lentils (the text says a cooked portion has about a third of these amounts).
servingState.squid: USDA record is raw squid; it is eaten cooked, and cooking changes the values.

unusualValues.bagel: Vitamin E of 7.5 mg per 100 g (about 52% of the reference per serving) is the USDA figure from two data points; unusually high for a plain bagel.
unusualValues.granola: Vitamin E of 11.1 mg per 100 g is a USDA estimate (no data points).
unusualValues.olives: Iron of 6.3 mg per 100 g (one data point) is high for canned olives.
unusualValues.mint: Iron of 11.9 mg per 100 g (two data points) is high; fresh herbs are eaten in tiny amounts.

safetyNotResearched.chocolate: Caffeine and theobromine content is not stated, and no source was read.
safetyNotResearched.spirulina: The catalogue cautions (contamination, pregnancy and autoimmune conditions) have no recorded source.
safetyNotResearched.asparagus: Vitamin K about 46 µg per serving, below the rule that adds the blood-thinner note (100 µg per 100 g); an editor may want it.
safetyNotResearched.fennel: Vitamin K about 55 µg per serving, below the rule that adds the blood-thinner note (100 µg per 100 g); an editor may want it.
safetyNotResearched.coconut-oil: No saturated-fat statement is made; an editor may decide whether one is needed.
safetyNotResearched.butter: No saturated-fat statement is made; an editor may decide whether one is needed.
safetyNotResearched.milk: Raw (unpasteurised) milk is not covered; the profile describes pasteurised milk.
safetyNotResearched.eggs: Raw or undercooked eggs are covered only by the cooking-temperature caution.

resolved.octopus: Vitamin B12 of 36 µg per 100 g is consistent with USDA's raw octopus record (20 µg per 100 g): the cooked value is 1.8 times the raw one, in line with water loss (USDA 174218 raw, 174249 cooked).
resolved.clam: Sodium of 1,200 mg per 100 g (cooked, moist heat) compares with 601 mg in USDA's raw mixed-species clam record (174214), a 2 times rise; the figures are USDA's own.
resolved.crab: Sodium of 1,070 mg per 100 g (cooked) compares with 836 mg in USDA's raw Alaska king crab record (175164).
resolved.shrimp: Sodium of 947 mg per 100 g (cooked) compares with 566 mg in the raw record (174210); both records carry the moisture-retention additives note.
resolved.scallop: Sodium of 667 mg per 100 g (steamed) compares with 392 mg in the raw record (174220).
resolved.almond-milk: All of the vitamin E (6.33 mg per 100 g) is listed by USDA as "Vitamin E, added", so it comes from fortification and varies by brand.
resolved.white-rice: Rice arsenic: added the FDA statement that rice tends to absorb more arsenic than other crops and can still be part of a well-balanced diet.
resolved.tuna: The mercury caution is now sourced: the FDA and EPA list "Tuna, canned light (includes skipjack)" as a Best Choice.
resolved.wheat: Opening line now says durum wheat (dry).
resolved.granola: Opening line now says homemade granola.
resolved.salsa: Opening line now says ready-to-serve salsa with salt.
resolved.red-snapper: Opening line now says the USDA record covers mixed species.

decisions.title: Dry-weight servings
decisions.question: These servings are for the dry food (USDA has no cooked record for most). Accept dry servings, clearly labelled, or switch to cooked records where they exist?

decisions.title: Raw squid record
decisions.question: USDA has raw and fried squid but no plainly cooked record. The raw values are shown with "cook before eating". Accept, use the fried record, or hold?

decisions.title: Record narrower than the catalogue name
decisions.question: sourdough-bread uses a French/Vienna bread record that includes sourdough; snapper and sea bass use mixed-species records. Accept with the record named, or rename the catalogue entries?

decisions.title: Tuna listed twice
decisions.question: Both entries use the same USDA record (canned light tuna in water). Keep both, merge, or distinguish them?
decisions.recommendation: Merge or distinguish at the catalogue level; profiles are identical in substance.

decisions.title: Vitamin E left out
decisions.question: USDA vitamin E for these is unusually high (7.5 and 11.1 mg per 100 g; granola is an estimate). Vitamin E is omitted from their key nutrients. Accept the omission?

decisions.title: High iron values from few data points
decisions.question: Iron of 6.3 and 11.9 mg per 100 g from one or two data points. Accept, or omit the iron highlight?
decisions.recommendation: Accept (8% of the reference per serving).

decisions.title: Chocolate
decisions.question: No caffeine or theobromine statement (no source read), and the dairy and soy tags depend on the product. Add a sourced note, and keep the tags?
decisions.recommendation: Keep the tags; decide on a caffeine note after a source is read.

decisions.title: Moderate vitamin K
decisions.question: About 46 and 55 µg of vitamin K per serving, below the 100 µg per 100 g rule that adds the blood-thinner note. Add the note?
decisions.recommendation: Leave as data; the existing rule is conservative enough.

decisions.title: Fat statements
decisions.question: No saturated-fat statement is made. Add a sourced one, or leave the data to speak?

decisions.title: Raw handling of milk and eggs
decisions.question: Profiles describe pasteurised milk and hard-boiled eggs. Add a sourced raw-milk or raw-egg line for people at greater risk (FDA)?
decisions.recommendation: Optional; a one-line FDA statement is available.

decisions.title: How sodium appears
decisions.question: Sodium is stored as data for every profile. A calm "nutrition note" appears only at 460 mg or more (the FDA's 20% of Daily Value "high" line). Food Detail has no notes field today. Show the note as a "Good to know" line, or keep it as data only?
decisions.recommendation: Keep as data; add the note only if Food Detail gains a place for it.

decisions.title: Allergen tags broader or narrower than the food
decisions.question: Coconut counted as a tree nut; tamari and miso gluten (many tamari are wheat-free); chocolate dairy and soy (product-dependent); sesame in bagels; celery and molluscs (EU lists, not on the US list of nine). Keep every tag (protective) or refine?
decisions.recommendation: Keep all tags; refine wording only with an allergist or label source.

decisions.title: Kidney bean boiling time
decisions.question: The inherited caution says "boil hard for 10 minutes". The FDA says soak at least 5 hours and boil in fresh water at least 30 minutes. The draft now uses the FDA wording. The app's own catalogue caution still has the 10-minute wording. Update the catalogue?
decisions.recommendation: Yes, as a safety correction (outside this audit; not changed).
